subject.title: fix: forward response-frame meta to clients

question: Should Gateway protocol v4 send optional top-level `res.meta` on existing response frames, or should response metadata wait for a version-gated or payload-scoped contract?
rationale: The code fix is narrow and now has live proof, but additive top-level response fields can affect strict generated clients outside the reference TypeScript and Swift clients.

options.title: Accept additive v4 `res.meta`
options.body: Land this after conflict resolution because the field is optional, documented, and reference clients tolerate it while clients that need metadata can finally read it.

options.title: Version-gate response metadata
options.body: Require a protocol-version or capability gate before sending `meta` if maintainers want to protect strict older clients from any new top-level response fields.

options.title: Use payload-specific metadata
options.body: Reject the envelope change and track a narrower per-method payload contract, trading compatibility caution for less reusable metadata plumbing.

recommendation.title: Accept additive v4 `res.meta`
recommendation.body: Land this after conflict resolution because the field is optional, documented, and reference clients tolerate it while clients that need metadata can finally read it.

likelyOwner.reason: The affected responder/schema/type lines and recent protocol work route most clearly to Vincent Koc for a v4 compatibility decision.
